Q: Matching multiple pairs of values between two tables; looking for an efficient maintainable method A:

First, about keyword search.
You can check each keyword as shown in your example using regexp.
Or you can split the "description" into separate words and search for a match (equality).
In my example used "string_to table" function to split description to words and then comparing with keywors for JOIN.

First part of query (splitting)

select *
from article_description ad
cross join lateral string_to_table(article_description,' ')w(word)

For first row we get

Next join (INNER) table "article_labels" to splitted words on "al.label_code=lk.label_code"

from article_description ad
cross join lateral string_to_table(article_description,' ')w(word)
inner join label_keywords lk on lk.keyword=w.word

Finally, we LEFT join existing pairs (label_code,keyword). If pair not exists,article_labels.article_code is null.

After JOIN we filter not matching rows (antijoin) by "where al.article_code is null"

With anti JOIN

select *
from article_description ad
cross join lateral string_to_table(article_description,' ')w(word)
inner join label_keywords lk on lk.keyword=w.word
left join article_labels al on al.label_code=lk.label_code and al.article_code=ad.article_code
   and al.locale=ad.locale
where al.article_code is null
;

Or with NOT EXISTS.

There we consider only articles, not having reference in "article_labels" table by columns(article_code,locale)

select *
from article_description ad
cross join lateral string_to_table(article_description,' ')w(word)
inner join label_keywords lk on lk.keyword=w.word
left join article_labels al on al.label_code=lk.label_code and al.article_code=ad.article_code
   and al.locale=ad.locale
where  not exists (select 1 from article_labels al2 where al2.article_code=ad.article_code and al2.locale=ad.locale)

Q: How can I tell which NSWindow triggered a breakpoint in a multi-window Mac app? A:

The memory address of an object is its unique identifier. It is how you tell when two objects are the same or different. That is the usual debugging workflow. If self is not a window but a view controller whose view is in the desired window, use self.view.window.

Q: Why Rust is taking a ton of my disk space and how to make it use less A:

Just to clarify: I wasn't suggesting someone buy a new laptop just for a hard drive. I was just trying to say that a midrange laptop's standard drive is in the 1TB range, meaning that if one were evaluating the impact of hundreds of gigabytes, it's reasonable to consider that as a proportion of 1TB. Sorry if that wasn't clear previously.

Q: Is Scrum useful for single programmer developments? A:

The single most important benefit of Scrum that is there even if there is just one developer is not the daily sync (meeting), but rather the limitation on context switches. While working in sprints this single developer can concentrate on given stories within his (presumably short) sprint knowing he won't be interrupted or pushed to do something else before finishing this.

Less context switching == less waste == more productivity.

BTW - Kanban offers less overhead than Scrum, but it is easier to circumvent and force developer to context switch. This can be a benefit but can easily become a problem too.

Q: Can I override Microsoft Access display default of four digits instead of two digits for calculated dates less than 50? A:

Convert to string using =Format([YourDateField], "yy") to always show just the last 2 digits of the year.

Q: Why is my program throwing an illegal instruction error? A:

Your compiler has literally inserted a "generate undefined instruction exception" instruction at the end of your int travelling(int bal) function because although it was declared to return an int, there is no return <some int value>; at all in it. That's "undefined behavior" (UB) and the compiler can do anything it wants, like deleting your computer's hard drive. It was being nice in this case though.

You can see the generated processor instructions for your C++ function in e.g. Godbolt's Compiler Explorer (https://godbolt.org/z/9GMKnjsT8), then you see that

  1. It generates the ud2 instruction (generate undefined instruction exception, see (https://mudongliang.github.io/x86/html/file_module_x86_id_318.html)

  2. It gives you a warning telling you what's wrong

Hence you should:

  • change your travelling() function to return void. It's just a print function and doesn't need to return anyhting.

  • check compiler warnings more thoroughly or compile with -pedantic to make the compiler refuse compilation when a warning occurs. Enable (most) of the warnings with -Wall -Wextra.
